transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hi. Um, I guess what brings me in is that I just keep making these really dumb mistakes at work. I'm a sales supervisor, and on our sales reports, I'll do things like copy the wrong numbers right off the team dashboard. Or I'll completely miss a line in a procedure I was supposed to check. And the thing is, it happens even when I thought I already went over it carefully. It's just getting to be a real problem.
Did you experience similar difficulties with attention and making careless mistakes when you were a child in school?

Yeah, I actually was like this as a kid, too. My mom still brings up the notes she'd get from my elementary school teachers. They were always saying that I rushed through my assignments, or that I lost my homework. And it wasn't just the work, either—they'd say I was always talking out of turn or that I couldn't just stay in my seat unless someone reminded me to sit down. So, yeah, it's been going on for a long time.
Nowadays as an adult, do you still often feel physically restless or have trouble sitting still?

Yeah, I do. Um, sitting through a long meeting at work is really tough. It almost feels like my body is just buzzing inside, if that makes sense. I end up having to shift around in my chair a lot, or I'll be tapping my foot. If it goes on too long, I usually just have to make some kind of excuse to get up and walk around for a second.
